title: Boolean Retrieval and the Inverted Index: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Boolean Retrieval and the Inverted Index: Visual Guide

1. From Merge To Postings | IR 100's two sorted arrays relabelled as two postings lists, with a slider over a rare term's document frequency comparing the m+n merge against reading two 100-million-bit matrix rows | query cost should scale with occurrences and not corpus size, but the merge bound is m+n so the longer list sets the floor

2. The Matrix Does Not Fit | the three-document incidence matrix with tappable term rows combined by AND or OR, plus sliders for corpus size and distinct terms per document showing 10^15 cells and 125 TB against 3 x 10^10 nonzero pairs | the matrix is the semantics and the postings list is the storage, and the 33,000x saving is decided by how few distinct terms one document holds

3. Build The Dictionary | a four-step walk from analysis to emitted (term, doc_id, position) tuples to the sort to the grouped dictionary and postings, with a payload toggle for doc IDs, term frequency and positions | indexing is a sorting problem: one sort makes equal terms adjacent and document IDs ascending at the same time, and every extra payload field is paid for

4. Two Cursors Stepping | the two-cursor algorithm stepped comparison by comparison over vector [1,3,7,10,14] and database [2,3,6,10,12,14] under AND, OR and AND NOT | emit on equality and otherwise advance the smaller cursor, bounded by m+n with constant state, and negation must ride on a positive candidate list rather than materialise a complement

5. Rarest Term First | the three-term conjunctive plan with df 80,000,000 / 2,000,000 / 5,000 reordered by hand and joined either by sequential merge or by probing the larger list | the AND result can never exceed the shortest list so rarest-first is provable, but the large win needs the right access method as well as the right order
